sentence: These communications were, as you would expect, biased--they were all in response to decisions to raise interest rates and most often occurred when those increases came shortly before an election.

sentence: We know that the short end of the yield curve is dominated by monetary policy and cyclical factors.
note: It is just explaining what affects the short end of the yield curve. No clear policy direction.

sentence: An extreme version of this view is that bubbles probably do not exist--that rational market processes always price assets at their fundamental value.
note: This is about the theory of asset bubbles, not really about whether rates should be raised or cut.

sentence: But the members generally were concerned that inflation might begin to rise over the intermediate term, especially if labor markets tightened further.
note: If inflation might rise and the labor market gets tighter, the Fed would have more reason to raise rates.

sentence: Putting It All Together I would now like to step back and consider the relative contributions to the trade deficit of each of the explanations I have discussed, as shown in figure 6.7 To the extent that the contributions of these shocks are reasonably well measured by the macroeconomic model simulations, the most important message I draw from them is that no single factor constitutes a dominant explanation of the deterioration in the U.S. current account balance.
note: It is explaining the causes of the trade deficit. There is no clear rate-policy direction.

sentence: With the Committee in the process of reviewing its monetary policy strategies and communication, and no additional accommodation being provided at this meeting, a few members indicated that they could support the Committee's decision even though they had not favored recent policy actions.
note: The phrase about no additional accommodation suggests policy is not becoming easier, which leans toward a tighter stance.

sentence: If the prices are wrong -- built on the base on an incorrect view of the economy or Federal Reserve intentions -- we will prove them wrong and provide an anchor for the market to adjust to.
note: This is mainly about correcting wrong market expectations. It does not clearly point to raising or cutting rates.

sentence: On the foreign trade side of the economy, an anticipated firming of economic conditions abroad would provide impetus to real net exports, At the same time, however, imports were expected to rise appreciably in response to the expansion of domestic economic activity and the appreciation of the dollar, and on balance the external sector probably would not be boosting real GDP.
note: It is describing trade and GDP effects, without a clear monetary-policy preference.

sentence: As we all know, starting in late February or March of last year, widespread economic and social lockdowns and other effects of the pandemic caused the swiftest and deepest contraction in employment and economic activity since the Great Depression.
note: A very severe economic contraction would normally make the Fed want to support the economy rather than tighten.

sentence: Participants agreed that the labor market had remained strong over the intermeeting period and that economic activity had risen at a moderate rate.
note: A strong labor market and moderate growth are just facts here. It does not clearly call for a policy move.

sentence: In their discussion of the balance-of-risks sentence in the press statement to be issued shortly after this meeting, all the members agreed that the latter should continue to express, as it had for every meeting earlier this year, their belief that the risks remained weighted toward rising inflation.
note: They are explicitly worried about inflation risks being tilted upward, which gives a reason to tighten.

sentence: To the extent that the combination of a low neutral rate, a flat Phillips curve, and low underlying inflation may lead financial imbalances to become more tightly linked to the business cycle, it is important to use tools other than monetary policy to temper the financial cycle.
note: It says financial imbalances should be handled with tools other than monetary policy, so there is no clear rate direction.

sentence: The several extensions of emergency unemployment insurance benefits appeared to have raised the measured unemployment rate, relative to levels recorded in past downturns, by encouraging some who have lost their jobs to remain in the labor force.
note: Higher unemployment and people remaining out of work point toward concern about jobs, which would make easing more attractive.

sentence: Communications about monetary policy over the intermeeting period generally had little effect on Treasury yields or the expected path of the federal funds rate.
note: This just says communications had little effect on rates. It does not imply a policy direction.

sentence: Rather, it is that the underlying sources of productivity growth are very complex.
note: This is simply saying productivity growth is complicated. No rate implication.

sentence: So, there has been impact through lower interest rates, but I think more broadly is the indirect effects.
note: It points to the positive effects of lower interest rates, which sounds supportive of easier policy.

sentence: Although in a number of sectors of the economy the imbalances between demand and supplyâ€”including labor supplyâ€”are substantial, I do continue to judge that these imbalances are likely to dissipate over time as the labor market and global supply chains eventually adjust and, importantly, do so without putting persistent upward pressure on price inflation, wage gains adjusted for productivity, and the 2 percent longer-run inflation objective.
note: The statement says the imbalances should fade without persistent inflation pressure, so there is less reason to raise rates.

sentence: Very low inflation and deflation pose qualitatively similar economic problems, though the magnitude of the associated costs can be expected to increase sharply as deflationary pressures intensify.
note: Very low inflation or deflation is described as an economic problem, so the Fed would be more inclined to support the economy.

sentence: Nonfarm payroll employment continued to expand through July and the civilian unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.
note: It is just reporting employment and unemployment numbers. No obvious rate direction by itself.

sentence: Indeed, few long-term inflation forecasts in any country currently exceed 5 percent,
note: Very low long-term inflation forecasts mean there is little inflation pressure pushing the Fed toward hikes.

sentence: Although higher energy and other costs had the potential to add to inflation pressure, core inflation had been relatively low in the preceding few months and longer-term inflation expectations remained contained.
note: There are inflation pressures, but they are described as temporary/contained. I would not read this as a clear hike signal.

sentence: Headline stock price indexes in the AFEs generally ended the period higher, whereas bank stocks in Europe declined.
note: This is just describing stock prices in different regions.

sentence: However, energy prices were expected to level out, and rents, while difficult to forecast, were viewed by some participants as likely to decelerate in coming quarters.
note: If energy prices level out and rents may slow, inflation pressure looks less threatening, reducing the need for hikes.

sentence: Several participants expressed the view that a decision regarding the long-run composition of the portfolio would not need to be made for some time, and a couple of participants highlighted the importance of making such a decision in the context of the ongoing review of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy strategies, tools, and communications practices.
note: This is about when to decide on the portfolio and the policy review, not a clear rate direction.

sentence: Although the economy has indeed strengthened over the past few quarters, job growth has been anemic and considerable slack persists in labor markets.
note: Weak job growth and considerable labor-market slack would make supporting employment more important.

sentence: Output was forecast to expand at a rate a little above the staff's estimate of its potential rate of growth in 2019 through 2021 and then to slow to a pace slightly below potential output growth in 2022.
note: Growth above potential can mean the economy is running hot, which could create a reason to tighten.

sentence: The broad index of the foreign exchange value of the dollar rose nearly 3 percent over the intermeeting period amid the rise in U. S. interest rates, market expectations that U. S. tax reform was becoming more likely, and foreign central bank actions and communications.
note: It describes the dollar rising alongside higher rates and other factors. It does not itself recommend a policy direction.

sentence: As always, my colleagues on the FOMC and I will act to foster our dual objectives of price stability and sustainable economic growth.
note: This is a general statement about the Fed's two goals, not whether it should raise or cut rates.

sentence: These participants cited, for example, the still-elevated levels of long-term unemployment and workers employed part time for economic reasons as well as low labor force participation.
note: High long-term unemployment, part-time workers and low participation suggest weakness in the labor market, supporting easier policy.

sentence: Put another way, the FOMC could have "preemptively" tightened monetary policy, based on forecasts, but recognizing the uncertainties about empirical relationships chose not to do so.
note: It directly discusses preemptively tightening policy. Even though they chose not to, the idea itself is clearly hawkish.

sentence: The effects of reduced monetary and fiscal policy stimulus were expected to be counterbalanced by continued low long-term interest rates and an abatement of energy-related headwinds.
note: Continued low long-term interest rates and less energy pressure suggest conditions are still supportive, leaning away from tightening.

sentence: If the FOMC were to tie mechanically our actions to market prices, then we would be placed in the sorry position of validating whatever whim that currently struck investors' fancy.
note: This is about not mechanically following asset prices. It does not say rates should go in either direction.

sentence: But it’s not easy to get a clear read on the implications of asset prices for the overall outlook.
note: It says asset prices are difficult to interpret. No clear policy direction.

sentence: In addition, some of the correlation may reflect the effect of the response of monetary policy to exchange rate developments.
note: This just describes how monetary policy can respond to exchange-rate movements. It does not say how policy should move.

sentence: However, as had been the case for many years, the members remained concerned that forecasts of money growth were still subject to a wide range of error in terms of the anticipated relationships between money growth and aggregate economic performance.
note: The problem described is uncertainty about money-growth relationships, not a direct argument for hikes or cuts.

sentence: core measures of consumer prices showed mixed changes on a twelve-month basis.
note: Mixed inflation changes do not clearly point in one policy direction.

sentence: Earlier in the year, as you will all recall, after careful study over a period of years, actually, the Committee announced the decision to implement monetary policy in an ample-reserves regime.
note: This is describing a change in the Fed's operating framework, not a rate preference.

sentence: Moreover, many members saw some risk that an easing move at this point might trigger a strong further advance in stock market prices that would not be justified on the basis of likely future earnings and could therefore lead to a relatively sharp and disruptive market adjustment later.
note: They worry that easing could push stock prices too high and cause problems later, which gives a reason to avoid cutting rates.

sentence: U.S. inflation remains muted.
note: Muted inflation means there is less pressure to raise rates and more room to keep policy easy.

sentence: Members agreed that they would continue to closely monitor inflation indicators and global economic and financial developments.
note: Monitoring inflation is normal policy behavior and does not say which way rates should move.

sentence: That means that we can run at low levels of unemployment and have a historically good—in some dimensions—labor market without having to worry about inflation.
note: If unemployment can stay low without causing inflation, the Fed would have less reason to raise rates.

sentence: No matter the near-term path of reducing accommodation, the FOMC must respond decisively to the data so as to maintain our credibility that we will bring down inflation.
note: It says the Fed must act decisively to bring inflation down, which strongly points toward tighter policy.

sentence: The System Open Market Account manager and the secretary will keep the Committee informed of ongoing developments regarding the System's balance sheet that could affect the attainment over time of the Committee's objectives of maximum employment and price stability. "
note: This is about monitoring the balance sheet and the Fed's objectives. No clear rate direction.

sentence: Compared with the baseline, the disruption to economic activity was more severe and protracted in this scenario, with real GDP and inflation lower and the unemployment rate higher by the end of the medium-term projection.
note: Lower GDP and inflation together with higher unemployment describe a weak economy, which would generally support easing.

sentence: That sentiment was apparently reinforced over the remainder of the period by the comments of several Federal Reserve officials and the release of the August employment report, which seemed to convey the view that the economy was emerging from its "soft patch. "
note: The economy emerging from a soft patch suggests improvement, but not necessarily enough to raise rates. I would read this as slightly supportive rather than clearly hawkish.

sentence: At the conclusion of the discussion, the Committee voted to authorize and direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until it was instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "The Federal Open Market Committee seeks monetary and financial conditions that will foster price stability and promote sustainable growth in output.
note: This is a general description of the policy objective of price stability and sustainable growth, not a specific rate direction.

sentence: In addition, coming to grips now with the outsized projected growth in entitlement spending in the early years of the next century could have a profound effect on current expectations of stability.
note: This is about entitlement spending and expectations of fiscal stability, not directly about monetary policy.

sentence: Participants commented that an increase in inflation from recent rates could have especially adverse effects on longer-run economic performance.
note: A rise in inflation is described as harmful to longer-run performance, which gives the Fed a reason to prevent inflation from rising.

sentence: However, with monetary policy assumed to remain highly accommodative, the staff continued to anticipate that real GDP growth would outpace that of potential over much of this period, leading to a decline in the unemployment rate to historically low levels.
note: Highly accommodative policy combined with growth above potential and historically low unemployment could make the Fed worry about overheating and consider tightening.

sentence: This supports the view that there has been an increase in trend productivity growth.
note: Higher productivity growth is generally positive, but this sentence alone does not clearly tell the Fed to raise or cut rates.
